claim: Zebrafish have an impressive capacity to regenerate neurons in the central nervous system.
source: Zebrafish have an impressive capacity to regenerate neurons in the central nervous system.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that draws from established scientific knowledge about zebrafish regenerative capacity.

claim: Regeneration of Purkinje cells is believed to be limited to developmental stages based on invasive lesions.
source: However, regeneration of the principal neuron of the evolutionary conserved cerebellum, the Purkinje cell (PC), is believed to be limited to developmental stages based on invasive lesions.
evidence: This statement references prior beliefs in the field, supported by citation to existing literature.

claim: The ablated larval PC population entirely recovers in number.
source: We demonstrate that the ablated larval PC population entirely recovers in number, quickly reestablishes electrophysiological properties, and properly integrates into circuits to regulate cerebellum-controlled behavior.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Regenerating larval PCs quickly reestablish electrophysiological properties.
source: We demonstrate that the ablated larval PC population entirely recovers in number, quickly reestablishes electrophysiological properties, and properly integrates into circuits to regulate cerebellum-controlled behavior.
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiological recordings presented in the manuscript.

claim: Regenerating larval PCs properly integrate into circuits to regulate cerebellum-controlled behavior.
source: We demonstrate that the ablated larval PC population entirely recovers in number, quickly reestablishes electrophysiological properties, and properly integrates into circuits to regulate cerebellum-controlled behavior.
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral analysis data presented in the manuscript.

claim: PC progenitors are present in larvae and adults.
source: PC progenitors are present in larvae and adults, and PC ablation in adult cerebelli results in an impressive PC regeneration of different PC subtypes able to restore behavioral impairments.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing ptf1a-expressing cells in both larvae and adults.

claim: PC ablation in adult cerebelli results in impressive PC regeneration of different PC subtypes.
source: PC progenitors are present in larvae and adults, and PC ablation in adult cerebelli results in an impressive PC regeneration of different PC subtypes able to restore behavioral impairments.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by quantitative analysis of PC regeneration in adult zebrafish.

claim: Regenerated adult PCs are able to restore behavioral impairments.
source: PC progenitors are present in larvae and adults, and PC ablation in adult cerebelli results in an impressive PC regeneration of different PC subtypes able to restore behavioral impairments.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral testing data showing recovery of exploratory behavior.

claim: Caudal PCs are more resistant to ablation than rostral PCs.
source: Interestingly, caudal PCs are more resistant to ablation and regenerate more efficiently, suggesting a rostro-caudal pattern of de- and regeneration properties.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of PC survival and regeneration in different cerebellar regions.

claim: Caudal PCs regenerate more efficiently than rostral PCs.
source: Interestingly, caudal PCs are more resistant to ablation and regenerate more efficiently, suggesting a rostro-caudal pattern of de- and regeneration properties.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of PC regeneration rates in different cerebellar regions.

claim: There is a rostro-caudal pattern of PC degeneration and regeneration properties.
source: Interestingly, caudal PCs are more resistant to ablation and regenerate more efficiently, suggesting a rostro-caudal pattern of de- and regeneration properties.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential resistance to ablation and regeneration efficiency observed along the rostro-caudal axis.

claim: The zebrafish cerebellum is able to regenerate functional PCs during all stages of the animal's life.
source: These findings demonstrate that the zebrafish cerebellum is able to regenerate functional PCs during all stages of the animal's life.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by data from both larval and adult zebrafish.

claim: Regeneration of neurons in the central nervous system of mammals is rare and limited to a few brain areas.
source: Regeneration of neurons in the central nervous system of mammals has been demonstrated to occur, but it is rare and limited to a few brain areas (Iismaa et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to existing literature.

claim: In some amphibians and fish, regeneration in almost any part of the central nervous system occurs during development, juvenile stages, and adulthood.
source: In contrast, in some amphibians and fish, regeneration in almost any part of the central nervous system is evident and occurs not only during development or in juveniles, but also during adulthood (Kizil et al., 2012; Lust and Tanaka, 2019; Tanaka and Reddien, 2011; Zambusi and Ninkovic, 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to existing literature.

claim: The zebrafish and mammalian cerebellum share nearly all neuronal cell types with conserved circuitry, physiology, and function.
source: The zebrafish and mammalian cerebellum share nearly all neuronal cell types with their circuitry, physiology, and function being conserved (Hashimoto and Hibi, 2012; Hibi et al., 2017; Koyama et al., 2021; Matsuda et al., 2017; Volkmann et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to existing literature.

claim: Purkinje cells, inhibitory interneurons, and eurydendroid cells in zebrafish arise from progenitor cells derived from the cerebellar ventricular zone expressing ptf1a.
source: For example, like in rodents, Purkinje cells (PCs), together with inhibitory interneurons and eurydendroid cells (ECs) – mammalian deep nuclei neuron equivalents – in zebrafish have been shown to arise from progenitor cells derived from the cerebellar ventricular zone (VZ) expressing the pancreas-associated transcription factor 1a (ptf1a) (Kani et al., 2010; Kaslin et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to existing literature.

claim: A first wave of postmitotic PCs appears from 3 to 6 days post-fertilization in zebrafish.
source: In zebrafish, a first wave of postmitotic PCs appears from 3 to 6 days post-fertilization (dpf), afterwards fewer PCs are added slowly over time to achieve a slow continuous increase in PC number aligned with larval growth (Bae et al., 2009; Hamling et al., 2015; Namikawa et al., 2019b).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to existing literature.

claim: After 6 dpf, fewer PCs are added slowly over time in zebrafish, achieving a slow continuous increase in PC number aligned with larval growth.
source: In zebrafish, a first wave of postmitotic PCs appears from 3 to 6 days post-fertilization (dpf), afterwards fewer PCs are added slowly over time to achieve a slow continuous increase in PC number aligned with larval growth (Bae et al., 2009; Hamling et al., 2015; Namikawa et al., 2019b).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to existing literature.

claim: Controversial reports exist about whether new PCs are still generated in the adult zebrafish cerebellum.
source: Controversial reports exist about whether in the adult zebrafish cerebellum new PCs are still generated (Kani et al., 2010; Kaslin et al., 2013; Kaslin et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement acknowledges conflicting findings in the literature, supported by citations.

claim: It is widely believed that all neurons within the zebrafish central nervous system are able to regenerate.
source: Based on the extensive adult neurogenesis and regenerative capacity, it is widely believed that all neurons within the zebrafish central nervous system are able to regenerate (Kroehne et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement describes a prevailing belief in the field, supported by citation.

claim: The long-held classical view that all zebrafish CNS neurons can regenerate has recently been challenged for Purkinje cells.
source: Yet, in elegant studies this long-held classical view has recently been upset for highly conserved key cerebellar neurons, the PCs (Kaslin et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement references recent findings that contradict the prevailing view, supported by citation.

claim: Purkinje cells constitute principal information processing neurons of the cerebellum.
source: PCs constitute principal information processing neurons of the cerebellum and provide direct output to neurons of the vestibular nuclei (Knogler et al., 2019; Namikawa et al., 2019a).
evidence: This is established knowledge about PC function, supported by citations.

claim: Purkinje cells provide direct output to neurons of the vestibular nuclei.
source: PCs constitute principal information processing neurons of the cerebellum and provide direct output to neurons of the vestibular nuclei (Knogler et al., 2019; Namikawa et al., 2019a).
evidence: This is established knowledge about PC connectivity, supported by citations.

claim: PC degeneration in humans results in severe neurological symptoms like ataxia, altered locomotor activity, anxiety, and social disabilities.
source: Hence, PC degeneration in humans results in severe neurological symptoms like ataxia, altered locomotor activity, but also anxiety and social disabilities (Fancellu et al., 2013; Schmitz-Hübsch et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement describes clinical manifestations of PC degeneration, supported by citations.

claim: PC degeneration diseases can be genetically modeled in zebrafish PCs.
source: These diseases can be genetically modeled in zebrafish PCs (Elsaey et al., 2021; Hsieh et al., 2020; Namikawa et al., 2019a; Namikawa et al., 2019b; Watchon et al., 2017), but it has remained elusive so far whether such PC degeneration can be counteracted by regeneration to slow down and mitigate disease progression.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to existing literature on zebrafish disease models.

claim: It has remained elusive whether PC degeneration can be counteracted by regeneration to slow down and mitigate disease progression.
source: These diseases can be genetically modeled in zebrafish PCs (Elsaey et al., 2021; Hsieh et al., 2020; Namikawa et al., 2019a; Namikawa et al., 2019b; Watchon et al., 2017), but it has remained elusive so far whether such PC degeneration can be counteracted by regeneration to slow down and mitigate disease progression.
evidence: This identifies a knowledge gap that the study addresses.

claim: During embryonic stages, the entire cerebellar primordium including PCs regenerates after surgical removal in zebrafish.
source: In zebrafish, during embryonic stages, the entire cerebellar primordium including PCs regenerates after surgical removal, due to repatterning processes in the hindbrain (Köster and Fraser, 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to existing literature.

claim: At larval and juvenile stages, the zebrafish cerebellum recovers from local wounding and regenerates PCs.
source: Also, at larval and juvenile stages, the cerebellum recovers from local wounding and regenerates PCs (Kaslin et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to existing literature.

claim: PC regeneration capacity declines and is lost at 3 months of age in zebrafish.
source: But this PC regeneration capacity declines and is lost at 3 months of age, which has been explained by the exhaustion of proper PC progenitors, while progenitors of other cerebellar neuronal cell types continue to undergo neurogenic divisions (Hentig et al., 2021; Kaslin et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement describes previous findings in the literature, supported by citations.

claim: The loss of PC regeneration capacity at 3 months has been explained by exhaustion of proper PC progenitors.
source: But this PC regeneration capacity declines and is lost at 3 months of age, which has been explained by the exhaustion of proper PC progenitors, while progenitors of other cerebellar neuronal cell types continue to undergo neurogenic divisions (Hentig et al., 2021; Kaslin et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement describes a hypothesis from previous literature, supported by citations.

claim: Progenitors of other cerebellar neuronal cell types continue to undergo neurogenic divisions after 3 months in zebrafish.
source: But this PC regeneration capacity declines and is lost at 3 months of age, which has been explained by the exhaustion of proper PC progenitors, while progenitors of other cerebellar neuronal cell types continue to undergo neurogenic divisions (Hentig et al., 2021; Kaslin et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to existing literature.

claim: The regeneration capacity of zebrafish PCs is limited, regenerating efficiently during larval and juvenile stages but lacking capacity during adulthood.
source: These findings comprehensively suggest that the regeneration capacity of zebrafish PCs is limited, regenerating efficiently during larval and juvenile stages as expected for teleostean neurons, but lacking such a capacity during adulthood resembling mammalian PCs (Kaslin et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement summarizes previous findings in the literature, supported by citation.

claim: Larval PC regeneration upon local wounding could represent ongoing growth of the PC population rather than a regenerative response.
source: Yet, larval PC regeneration upon local wounding has been based on the appearance of new PCs, but this could represent ongoing growth of the PC population rather than a regenerative response.
evidence: This is a critical interpretation of previous findings, based on logical inference.

claim: PCs considered to have regenerated cannot be distinguished from non-injured neighbors in previous studies.
source: In addition, PCs considered to have regenerated cannot be distinguished from non-injured neighbors, therefore the proper physiological integration of regenerated larval PCs into existing circuitry could not be revealed, therefore also in larvae functional PC regeneration is still in question (Hentig et al., 2021; Kaslin et al., 2017).
evidence: This identifies a limitation of previous studies, supported by citations.

claim: The proper physiological integration of regenerated larval PCs into existing circuitry could not be revealed in previous studies.
source: In addition, PCs considered to have regenerated cannot be distinguished from non-injured neighbors, therefore the proper physiological integration of regenerated larval PCs into existing circuitry could not be revealed, therefore also in larvae functional PC regeneration is still in question (Hentig et al., 2021; Kaslin et al., 2017).
evidence: This identifies a knowledge gap in previous studies, supported by citations.

claim: Functional PC regeneration in larvae is still in question.
source: In addition, PCs considered to have regenerated cannot be distinguished from non-injured neighbors, therefore the proper physiological integration of regenerated larval PCs into existing circuitry could not be revealed, therefore also in larvae functional PC regeneration is still in question (Hentig et al., 2021; Kaslin et al., 2017).
evidence: This identifies a knowledge gap that the study addresses.

claim: Extensive surgical ablations remove important progenitors and the cellular and extracellular environment likely required for PC regeneration.
source: Extensive surgical ablations remove important progenitors and the cellular and extracellular environment likely required for PC regeneration.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the limitations of surgical ablation approaches.

claim: Local traumatic injuries may be counteracted by plasticity of neighboring PCs.
source: Local traumatic injuries instead may be counteracted by plasticity of neighboring PCs.
evidence: This is a logical inference about potential confounding factors in injury studies.

claim: Acute traumatic cerebellum injuries affect numerous cell types beyond PCs in a defined area.
source: In addition, acute traumatic cerebellum injuries affect numerous cell types beyond PCs in a defined area, and if invasive, induce wound healing that could influence regeneration (Hentig et al., 2021; Kaslin et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a logical inference about the complexity of injury responses, supported by citations.

claim: Invasive injuries induce wound healing that could influence regeneration.
source: In addition, acute traumatic cerebellum injuries affect numerous cell types beyond PCs in a defined area, and if invasive, induce wound healing that could influence regeneration (Hentig et al., 2021; Kaslin et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a logical inference about potential confounding factors in injury studies, supported by citations.

claim: Degenerative diseases of PCs affect the entire population of a single-cell type by non-invasive cell death mechanisms.
source: Instead, degenerative diseases of PCs affect the entire population of a single-cell type by non-invasive cell death mechanisms (Meera et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement describes characteristics of neurodegenerative diseases, supported by citation.

claim: Different situations of PC loss (injury vs. degeneration) pose different demands and constraints on regeneration.
source: Likely, these principally different situations of PC loss pose different demands and constraints on regeneration.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the differences between injury and degeneration models.

claim: The ability of larval and adult PCs to regenerate is still enigmatic.
source: Therefore, the ability of larval and adult PCs to regenerate is still enigmatic.
evidence: This identifies the knowledge gap that motivates the study.

claim: Transgenic PC-ATTAC zebrafish allow selective ablation of PCs by apoptosis through non-invasive administration of Tamoxifen.
source: We have recently introduced transgenic PC-ATTAC zebrafish, in which PCs can be selectively ablated by apoptosis through non-invasive administration of Tamoxifen (Weber et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes a previously published tool, supported by citation.

claim: Ablating nearly the entire PC population uncouples plasticity from regeneration and creates a high regenerative demand.
source: (1) Ablating nearly the entire PC population uncouples plasticity from regeneration and creates a high regenerative demand;
evidence: This is a logical inference about the advantages of the PC-ATTAC model.

claim: PC death by apoptosis and microglia phagocytosis prevents leakage of PC contents into the extracellular environment and resembles disease-associated neurodegeneration.
source: (2) PC death by apoptosis and microglia phagocytosis (Weber et al., 2016) prevents leakage of PC contents into the extracellular environment and resembles disease-associated neurodegeneration and;
evidence: This describes a characteristic of the PC-ATTAC model, supported by citation and logical inference.

claim: Fluorescent protein expression in PCs allows for quantifying ablation and recovery efficiencies.
source: (3) Fluorescent protein expression in PCs allows not only for quantifying ablation and recovery efficiencies, but also for investigating physiological integrity of regenerating PCs (Hsieh et al., 2014) and relating behavioral recovery to the extent of PC population regrowth (Champagne et al., 2010; Huang and Neuhauss, 2008);
evidence: This describes an advantage of the PC-ATTAC model, supported by citations.

claim: Fluorescent protein expression in PCs allows for investigating physiological integrity of regenerating PCs.
source: (3) Fluorescent protein expression in PCs allows not only for quantifying ablation and recovery efficiencies, but also for investigating physiological integrity of regenerating PCs (Hsieh et al., 2014) and relating behavioral recovery to the extent of PC population regrowth (Champagne et al., 2010; Huang and Neuhauss, 2008);
evidence: This describes an advantage of the PC-ATTAC model, supported by citation.

claim: Fluorescent protein expression in PCs allows for relating behavioral recovery to the extent of PC population regrowth.
source: (3) Fluorescent protein expression in PCs allows not only for quantifying ablation and recovery efficiencies, but also for investigating physiological integrity of regenerating PCs (Hsieh et al., 2014) and relating behavioral recovery to the extent of PC population regrowth (Champagne et al., 2010; Huang and Neuhauss, 2008);
evidence: This describes an advantage of the PC-ATTAC model, supported by citations.

claim: Age-independent Tamoxifen treatment allows study of PC regeneration in larvae, juveniles, and adults under equivalent conditions.
source: (4) Age-independent Tamoxifen treatment allows to study PC regeneration in larvae, juveniles, and adults under equivalent conditions.
evidence: This describes an advantage of the PC-ATTAC model based on logical inference.

claim: PC-ATTAC carriers express membrane-targeted red fluorescent protein (FyntagRFP-T) as a reporter together with Tamoxifen-inducible Caspase 8 selectively in postmitotic cerebellar Purkinje neurons.
source: Carriers of the stable transgenic zebrafish strain PC-ATTAC express a membrane-targeted red fluorescent protein (FyntagRFP-T) as a reporter together with a Tamoxifen-inducible Caspase 8 selectively in postmitotic cerebellar Purkinje neurons (Figure 1A; Weber et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes the PC-ATTAC transgenic construct, supported by citation and figure reference.

claim: Between 4 and 6 days post-fertilization the PC layer in zebrafish is established and matures.
source: Between 4 and 6 days post-fertilization (dpf) the PC layer in zebrafish is established and matures (Hamling et al., 2015; Namikawa et al., 2019b).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to existing literature.

claim: Incubation of PC-ATTAC larvae between 4 and 6 dpf with 4-OHT overnight induced apoptosis in 85-95% of PCs.
source: Incubation of PC-ATTAC larvae between 4 and 6 dpf with 4-hydroxy-tamoxifen (4-OHT) overnight induced apoptosis in the majority of PCs (85–95%) leaving red fluorescent apoptotic debris behind, which progressively disappeared by microglial phagocytosis within 3–5 days post-treatment (dpt) (Weber et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes experimental results, supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Red fluorescent apoptotic debris from ablated PCs progressively disappeared by microglial phagocytosis within 3-5 days post-treatment.
source: Incubation of PC-ATTAC larvae between 4 and 6 dpf with 4-hydroxy-tamoxifen (4-OHT) overnight induced apoptosis in the majority of PCs (85–95%) leaving red fluorescent apoptotic debris behind, which progressively disappeared by microglial phagocytosis within 3–5 days post-treatment (dpt) (Weber et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes experimental observations, supported by citation to previous work.

claim: EtOH-treated control specimens did not show any sign of PC death.
source: Since ethanol (EtOH) was used as a solvent for 4-OHT stock solutions, EtOH-treated (0.4% final concentration) specimens were used as controls, which did not show any sign of PC death (Figure 1B).
evidence: This describes control experimental results, supported by figure reference.

claim: About 5-7 days post-treatment, first red fluorescent PCs reappeared after ablation.
source: About 5–7 dpt first red fluorescent PCs reappeared, and already after about 11 dpt nearly half of the PC population compared to controls was replenished (Figure 1B, C).
evidence: This describes experimental observations, supported by figure reference.

claim: After about 11 days post-treatment, nearly half of the PC population compared to controls was replenished.
source: About 5–7 dpt first red fluorescent PCs reappeared, and already after about 11 dpt nearly half of the PC population compared to controls was replenished (Figure 1B, C).
evidence: This describes experimental observations, supported by figure reference.

claim: During larval stages the PC population can quickly recover from a nearly complete removal.
source: This demonstrates that during larval stages the PC population can quickly recover from a nearly complete removal.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: PC numbers in ablated specimens reached 70% of controls at 1 month post-treatment.
source: Compared to PCs found in non-ablated controls, numbers of PCs in specimens after initial PC ablation reached 70% at 1 mpt, 91% at 3 mpt, and 100% at 6 mpt, respectively (Figure 1D–F).
evidence: This describes quantitative experimental results, supported by figure reference.

claim: PC numbers in ablated specimens reached 91% of controls at 3 months post-treatment.
source: Compared to PCs found in non-ablated controls, numbers of PCs in specimens after initial PC ablation reached 70% at 1 mpt, 91% at 3 mpt, and 100% at 6 mpt, respectively (Figure 1D–F).
evidence: This describes quantitative experimental results, supported by figure reference.

claim: PC numbers in ablated specimens reached 100% of controls at 6 months post-treatment.
source: Compared to PCs found in non-ablated controls, numbers of PCs in specimens after initial PC ablation reached 70% at 1 mpt, 91% at 3 mpt, and 100% at 6 mpt, respectively (Figure 1D–F).
evidence: This describes quantitative experimental results, supported by figure reference.

claim: PCs ablated during larval development amount to about one quarter of the adult PC population at 6 months.
source: Since PCs ablated during larval development (ca. 400) amount to about one quarter of the adult PC population at 6 months (ca 1500), an obvious reduction in PC population size would be expected, if the ablated PCs were not replaced, but such a reduction in PC numbers was not observed.
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the experimental data.

claim: A full recovery of PCs was evident at 6 months post-treatment.
source: Instead, a full recovery of PCs was evident at 6 mpt.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: No apparent anatomical differences of the cerebellar cortex at 1 and 6 months post-treatment could be observed by immunohistochemistry against ZebrinII on sagittal sections from PC-ablated and control specimens.
source: In addition, no apparent anatomical differences of the cerebellar cortex at 1 and 6 mpt could be observed by immunohistochemistry against the PC-specific antigen ZebrinII on sagittal sections from PC-ablated and control specimens (Figure 1G).
evidence: This describes experimental observations, supported by figure reference.

claim: Quantification of the distance between anterior and posterior PCs in the PC layer on sagittal sections revealed no significant differences between PC-ablated and control specimens at 1, 3, and 6 months post-treatment.
source: In addition, quantification of the distance between anterior and posterior PCs in the PC layer on sagittal sections through the corpus cerebelli (CCe) of PC-ablated and control specimens at 1, 3, and 6 mpt revealed no significant differences (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This describes quantitative experimental results, supported by figure reference.

claim: During the first 7 days post-ablation no significant increase in proliferating cell numbers could be observed in PC-ablated larvae compared to EtOH-treated controls.
source: During the first 7 days post-ablation no significant increase in proliferating cell numbers could be observed in PC-ablated larvae compared to EtOH-treated controls (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–D).
evidence: This describes experimental results from BrdU labeling, supported by figure reference.

claim: BrdU treatment at 18 days post-treatment showed the same result as earlier time points (no significant increase in proliferating cells).
source: The same result was obtained when this BrdU treatment was repeated around 2 weeks later at 18 dpt (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–G).
evidence: This describes experimental results from BrdU labeling, supported by figure reference.

claim: A second pulse of EdU 4 days later at 22 days post-treatment revealed a much lower number of BrdU/EdU double-positive cells at 26 days post-treatment.
source: A second pulse of 5-Ethynyl-2′-deoxyuridine (EdU) 4 days later at 22 dpt revealed a much lower number of BrdU/EdU double-positive cells at 26 dpt, indicating that most of the newly generated PC progenitors passed on to differentiation.
evidence: This describes experimental results from double labeling, supported by figure reference.

claim: Most newly generated PC progenitors passed on to differentiation rather than continuing to proliferate.
source: A second pulse of 5-Ethynyl-2′-deoxyuridine (EdU) 4 days later at 22 dpt revealed a much lower number of BrdU/EdU double-positive cells at 26 dpt, indicating that most of the newly generated PC progenitors passed on to differentiation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the double labeling data.

claim: In PC-ablated specimens the number of BrdU/EdU double-positive cells was significantly elevated compared to controls.
source: However, in PC-ablated specimens the number of BrdU/EdU double-positive cells was significantly elevated suggesting that PC progenitors add on average more PCs to the PC layer by additional rounds of proliferation in PC-ablated zebrafish (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–H).
evidence: This describes quantitative experimental results, supported by figure reference.

claim: PC progenitors add on average more PCs to the PC layer by additional rounds of proliferation in PC-ablated zebrafish.
source: However, in PC-ablated specimens the number of BrdU/EdU double-positive cells was significantly elevated suggesting that PC progenitors add on average more PCs to the PC layer by additional rounds of proliferation in PC-ablated zebrafish (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–H).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the double labeling data.

claim: PC regeneration was neither initiated nor later promoted by a burst in cell proliferation.
source: Together these findings show that PC regeneration was neither initiated nor later promoted by a burst in cell proliferation, but occurred continuously by slowly adding surplus PCs over time via a delayed cell cycle exit until the full PC population size was reestablished 6 months later.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the proliferation data.

claim: PC regeneration occurred continuously by slowly adding surplus PCs over time via a delayed cell cycle exit until the full PC population size was reestablished 6 months later.
source: Together these findings show that PC regeneration was neither initiated nor later promoted by a burst in cell proliferation, but occurred continuously by slowly adding surplus PCs over time via a delayed cell cycle exit until the full PC population size was reestablished 6 months later.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the proliferation and PC quantification data.

claim: After PC ablation, none of the reappearing PCs expressed both gfap:EGFP and PC-ATTAC fluorescent reporters.
source: Yet, after PC ablation none of the reappearing PCs expressed both fluorescent reporters (Figure 2A), nor did the radial glia cell population increase significantly (Figure 2B).
evidence: This describes experimental observations from double transgenic analysis, supported by figure reference.

claim: The radial glia cell population did not increase significantly after PC ablation.
source: Yet, after PC ablation none of the reappearing PCs expressed both fluorescent reporters (Figure 2A), nor did the radial glia cell population increase significantly (Figure 2B).
evidence: This describes quantitative experimental results, supported by figure reference.

claim: Immunohistochemistry using anti-Blbp antibody showed coexpression in 90% of gfap:GFP-positive radial glia in control larvae.
source: Immunohistochemistry in control larvae using an antibody against brain lipid-binding protein (Blbp) expressed in radial glia showed coexpression in 90% of gfap:GFP-positive radial glia, but also failed to detect Blbp expression in PCs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes experimental results from immunohistochemistry, supported by figure reference.

claim: Anti-Blbp antibody failed to detect Blbp expression in PCs.
source: Immunohistochemistry in control larvae using an antibody against brain lipid-binding protein (Blbp) expressed in radial glia showed coexpression in 90% of gfap:GFP-positive radial glia, but also failed to detect Blbp expression in PCs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes experimental results from immunohistochemistry, supported by figure reference.

claim: The contribution of radial glia to larval PC differentiation and regeneration is unlikely.
source: This makes the contribution of radial glia to larval PC differentiation and regeneration unlikely, although it cannot be excluded that gfap-enhancer-driven EGFP expression had been lost by the time regenerating PCs differentiate.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data, with acknowledgment of alternative explanations.

claim: It cannot be excluded that gfap-enhancer-driven EGFP expression had been lost by the time regenerating PCs differentiate.
source: This makes the contribution of radial glia to larval PC differentiation and regeneration unlikely, although it cannot be excluded that gfap-enhancer-driven EGFP expression had been lost by the time regenerating PCs differentiate.
evidence: This acknowledges a limitation of the experimental approach.

claim: VZ-derived neuroepithelial cells expressing Ptf1a give rise to GABAergic cerebellar neurons including PCs in mammals and zebrafish.
source: As an alternative, VZ-derived neuroepithelial cells were tested that give rise to GABAergic cerebellar neurons. These VZ-derived progenitors express the transcription factor Ptf1a and among others give rise to PCs in mammals as well as in zebrafish (Hoshino et al., 2005; Kani et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to existing literature.

claim: Transient green fluorescent protein expression in Tg(ptf1a:EGFP) can be used for monitoring VZ-derived progenitor cells.
source: Hence, transient green fluorescent protein expression in the transgenic strain Tg(ptf1a:EGFP) can be used for monitoring these VZ-derived progenitor cells (Bae et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to existing literature.

claim: Double fluorescent PCs (ptf1a:EGFP and PC-ATTAC) were observed following PC ablation.
source: Indeed, double fluorescent PCs in Tg(ptf1a:EGFP) larvae in the PC-ATTAC background were observed following PC ablation (Figure 2C–E) and were significantly increased in their ratio compared to only red fluorescent PCs for about 2 weeks starting two days after ablation (Figure 2F, G).
evidence: This describes experimental observations, supported by figure reference.

claim: Double fluorescent PCs were significantly increased in their ratio compared to only red fluorescent PCs for about 2 weeks starting two days after ablation.
source: Indeed, double fluorescent PCs in Tg(ptf1a:EGFP) larvae in the PC-ATTAC background were observed following PC ablation (Figure 2C–E) and were significantly increased in their ratio compared to only red fluorescent PCs for about 2 weeks starting two days after ablation (Figure 2F, G).
evidence: This describes quantitative experimental results, supported by figure reference.

claim: The ratio of double fluorescent PCs is in favor of newly differentiated PCs, as EGFP expression by the ptf1a enhancer is only transient.
source: The ratio of double fluorescent PCs is in favor of newly differentiated PCs, as EGFP expression by the ptf1a enhancer is only transient.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the double fluorescent PC data based on known properties of the ptf1a enhancer.

claim: Mature PCs in control specimens exceed mature PC numbers in larvae with active PC regeneration.
source: Mature PCs in control specimens therefore, exceed mature PC numbers in larvae with active PC regeneration (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This describes quantitative experimental results, supported by figure reference.

claim: The absolute number of ptf1a:EGFP-expressing cells in the cerebellum was not significantly higher in PC-ablated PC-ATTAC larvae compared to controls.
source: The absolute number of ptf1a:EGFP-expressing cells in the cerebellum was not significantly higher in PC-ablated PC-ATTAC larvae compared to controls (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B) consistent with the BrdU labeling results.
evidence: This describes quantitative experimental results, supported by figure reference.

claim: A small increase in green fluorescent PC progenitor cells may be masked as ptf1a:EGFP-expressing cells contribute to several neuronal lineages of the cerebellum.
source: In addition, a small increase in green fluorescent PC progenitor cells may be further masked as ptf1a:EGFP-expressing cells contribute to several neuronal lineages of the cerebellum (Bae et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a logical inference about potential masking effects, supported by citation.

claim: Larval PC regeneration is driven by a small increase of VZ-derived ptf1a-expressing neuroepithelial cells, the natural PC progenitor population.
source: In conclusion, larval PC regeneration is driven by a small increase of VZ-derived ptf1a-expressing neuroepithelial cells, the natural PC progenitor population.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ptf1a:EGFP and proliferation data.

claim: Only a small fraction of ptf1a:GFP cells (about 10%) were found to coexpress Blbp.
source: While radial glia could act as progenitors of ptf1a:GFP-positive VZ-derived neurons and therefore also of regenerating PCs, only a small fraction of ptf1a:GFP cells of about 10% were found to coexpress Blbp, with an even smaller fraction of olig2:GFP-positive cells displaying coexpression of Blbp, which likely present ptf1a-derived progenitors of oligodendrocytes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes quantitative experimental results, supported by figure reference.

claim: An even smaller fraction of olig2:GFP-positive cells displayed coexpression of Blbp, which likely represent ptf1a-derived progenitors of oligodendrocytes.
source: While radial glia could act as progenitors of ptf1a:GFP-positive VZ-derived neurons and therefore also of regenerating PCs, only a small fraction of ptf1a:GFP cells of about 10% were found to coexpress Blbp, with an even smaller fraction of olig2:GFP-positive cells displaying coexpression of Blbp, which likely present ptf1a-derived progenitors of oligodendrocytes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the coexpression data, supported by figure reference.

claim: Progenitors of regenerating PCs are unlikely to be derived from radial glia expressing gfap or Blbp.
source: Hence, progenitors of regenerating PCs are unlikely to be derived from radial glia-expressing gfap or Blbp or have lost gfap-enhancer-driven EGFP expression despite the long half-life of the GFP protein (Li et al., 1998) at the time of PC differentiation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the coexpression data, with acknowledgment of alternative explanations and citation.

claim: Unambiguous clarification of the early progenitors of regenerating PCs has to await precise genetic fate mapping tools for permanently tracing radial glia derivatives in the zebrafish cerebellum.
source: Unambiguous clarification of the early progenitors of regenerating PCs has to await precise genetic fate mapping tools for permanently tracing radial glia derivatives in the zebrafish cerebellum.
evidence: This acknowledges a limitation of the current study and suggests future directions.

claim: Both double fluorescent recently differentiated PCs and regenerating PCs marked by cumulative BrdU labeling were not randomly distributed, but clustered loosely in two domains along the dorsal midline and in lateral parts of the cerebellum.
source: Interestingly, both double fluorescent recently differentiated PCs (Figure 2D, E) and regenerating PCs marked by cumulative BrdU labeling (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C) were not randomly distributed, but clustered loosely in two domains along the dorsal midline and in lateral parts of the cerebellum, respectively.
evidence: This describes spatial patterns observed in the experimental data, supported by figure references.

claim: The spatial pattern of regenerating PCs suggests that the VZ is spatially patterned like the adjacent germinal zone of the upper rhombic lip.
source: This suggests that the VZ is spatially patterned like the adjacent germinal zone of the upper rhombic lip (Volkmann et al., 2008).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the spatial distribution data, supported by citation.

claim: Differentiating PCs require about two days to establish a stable firing pattern of a mature PC with an average firing frequency between 8 and 10 Hz.
source: These studies confirmed that differentiating PCs require about two days to establish a stable firing pattern of a mature PC with an average firing frequency between 8 and 10 Hz, displaying high-frequency bursts of over 30 Hz and a ratio for complex spikes to simple spikes (cs/ss) of 0.04 (Harmon et al., 2017; Hsieh et al., 2014; Scalise et al., 2016; Sengupta and Thirumalai, 2015).
evidence: This describes electrophysiological reference data, supported by citations.

claim: Mature PCs display high-frequency bursts of over 30 Hz.
source: These studies confirmed that differentiating PCs require about two days to establish a stable firing pattern of a mature PC with an average firing frequency between 8 and 10 Hz, displaying high-frequency bursts of over 30 Hz and a ratio for complex spikes to simple spikes (cs/ss) of 0.04 (Harmon et al., 2017; Hsieh et al., 2014; Scalise et al., 2016; Sengupta and Thirumalai, 2015).
evidence: This describes electrophysiological reference data, supported by citations.

claim: Mature PCs have a ratio for complex spikes to simple spikes (cs/ss) of 0.04.
source: These studies confirmed that differentiating PCs require about two days to establish a stable firing pattern of a mature PC with an average firing frequency between 8 and 10 Hz, displaying high-frequency bursts of over 30 Hz and a ratio for complex spikes to simple spikes (cs/ss) of 0.04 (Harmon et al., 2017; Hsieh et al., 2014; Scalise et al., 2016; Sengupta and Thirumalai, 2015).
evidence: This describes electrophysiological reference data, supported by citations.

claim: First PCs born from 4-6 dpf forming the initial PC layer reach a plateau of electrophysiological maturity around 8 dpf.
source: First PCs born from 4–6 dpf forming the initial PC layer reach a plateau of electrophysiological maturity around 8 dpf (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This describes electrophysiological reference data, supported by figure reference.

claim: During the acute phase of PC degeneration and debris clearance (0-4 dpt), the average frequency and bursting frequency of few remaining PCs in PC-ablated larvae were significantly lower compared to controls.
source: During the acute phase of PC degeneration and debris clearance (0–4 dpt), the average frequency and the bursting frequency of few remaining PCs in PC-ablated larvae were significantly lower compared to controls and also the cs/ss ratio was elevated in an obvious trend (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E–G).
evidence: This describes electrophysiological experimental results, supported by figure reference.

claim: During the acute phase of PC degeneration (0-4 dpt), the cs/ss ratio was elevated in an obvious trend.
source: During the acute phase of PC degeneration and debris clearance (0–4 dpt), the average frequency and the bursting frequency of few remaining PCs in PC-ablated larvae were significantly lower compared to controls and also the cs/ss ratio was elevated in an obvious trend (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E–G).
evidence: This describes electrophysiological experimental results, supported by figure reference.

claim: During the acute regeneration phase (5-10 dpt), increasing numbers of PCs displayed characteristic simple and complex spike patterns.
source: During the acute regeneration phase (5–10 dpt) increasing numbers of PCs displayed characteristic simple and complex spike patterns (Figure 3B, B') with the average tonic firing and spontaneous burst frequencies steadily increasing to normal mature PC values.
evidence: This describes electrophysiological experimental results, supported by figure reference.

claim: During the acute regeneration phase (5-10 dpt), the average tonic firing and spontaneous burst frequencies steadily increased to normal mature PC values.
source: During the acute regeneration phase (5–10 dpt) increasing numbers of PCs displayed characteristic simple and complex spike patterns (Figure 3B, B') with the average tonic firing and spontaneous burst frequencies steadily increasing to normal mature PC values.
evidence: This describes electrophysiological experimental results, supported by figure reference.

claim: During the acute regeneration phase (5-10 dpt), the cs/ss ratio after an initial increase reestablished ratios of mature PCs.
source: Similarly, the cs/ss ratio after an initial increase, reestablished ratios of mature PCs.
evidence: This describes electrophysiological experimental results.

claim: During the extended regeneration period (10-21 dpt), the average tonic firing frequency and cs/ss ratio remained stable and compared well to mature control PCs.
source: During the extended regeneration period (10–21 dpt) the average tonic firing frequency and cs/ss ratio remained stable and compared well to mature control PCs.
evidence: This describes electrophysiological experimental results.

claim: Regenerating PCs successfully integrated into the remaining cerebellar network.
source: This indicates that regenerating PCs successfully integrated into the remaining cerebellar network and regenerated PCs were indistinguishable from controls at 10 dpt.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the electrophysiological data.

claim: Regenerated PCs were indistinguishable from controls at 10 days post-treatment.
source: This indicates that regenerating PCs successfully integrated into the remaining cerebellar network and regenerated PCs were indistinguishable from controls at 10 dpt.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the electrophysiological data.

claim: The average spontaneous burst frequency of regenerated PCs was increased by 1.5-fold compared to controls at 21 days post-treatment.
source: Of note, the average spontaneous burst frequency of regenerated PCs was increased by 1.5-fold in regenerated PCs compared to controls at 21 dpt (Figure 3D), suggestive of a possible compensatory mechanism (see discussion).
evidence: This describes quantitative electrophysiological results, supported by figure reference.

claim: The increased burst frequency in regenerated PCs at 21 dpt is suggestive of a possible compensatory mechanism.
source: Of note, the average spontaneous burst frequency of regenerated PCs was increased by 1.5-fold in regenerated PCs compared to controls at 21 dpt (Figure 3D), suggestive of a possible compensatory mechanism (see discussion).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the electrophysiological data.

claim: A second Tamoxifen treatment at 10 days post-treatment resulted in reduction of the PC population to about 6%.
source: Yet, such a second Tamoxifen treatment at 10 dpt when about half of the PC population had been reestablished, resulted again in the reduction of the PC population to about 6% (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This describes experimental results from repeated ablation, supported by figure reference.

claim: After the second ablation, physiological measurements revealed a significant decrease in average firing and bursting frequency and a significant increase in the cs/ss ratio of the remaining PCs.
source: Physiological measurements revealed – similar to the first ablation period – a significant decrease in average firing and bursting frequency and a significant increase in the cs/ss ratio of the remaining PCs.
evidence: This describes electrophysiological results from repeated ablation.

claim: Within 10 days after the repeated ablation, the PC population recovered to about 64% compared to PC numbers in age-matched control larvae.
source: Within the following 10 days the PC population recovered from the repeated ablation to about 64% compared to PC numbers in age-matched control larvae, and the physiological signatures of the average firing frequency and cs/ss ratio returned to values indistinguishable from non-ablated PCs in control specimens (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This describes quantitative results from repeated ablation, supported by figure reference.

claim: After repeated ablation, the physiological signatures of the average firing frequency and cs/ss ratio returned to values indistinguishable from non-ablated PCs in control specimens.
source: Within the following 10 days the PC population recovered from the repeated ablation to about 64% compared to PC numbers in age-matched control larvae, and the physiological signatures of the average firing frequency and cs/ss ratio returned to values indistinguishable from non-ablated PCs in control specimens (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This describes electrophysiological results from repeated ablation, supported by figure reference.

claim: The repeated ablation findings argue strongly against a physiological recovery of the ablated PC population solely by plasticity mechanisms.
source: These findings argue strongly against a physiological recovery of the ablated PC population solely by plasticity mechanisms and indicate that this recovery is majorly driven by newly added regenerating PCs that properly reintegrate into the cerebellar circuitry.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the repeated ablation data.

claim: Physiological recovery is majorly driven by newly added regenerating PCs that properly reintegrate into the cerebellar circuitry.
source: These findings argue strongly against a physiological recovery of the ablated PC population solely by plasticity mechanisms and indicate that this recovery is majorly driven by newly added regenerating PCs that properly reintegrate into the cerebellar circuitry.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the repeated ablation data.

claim: ECs are the principal direct efferences of zebrafish PCs and represent the neuronal equivalent of deep cerebellar nuclei neurons in mammals.
source: ECs are the principal direct efferences of zebrafish PCs and represent the neuronal equivalent of deep cerebellar nuclei neurons in mammals (Heap et al., 2013; Matsui et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge about EC function, supported by citations.

claim: No difference in EC number between PC-ablated and control larvae could be observed.
source: When green fluorescent ECs were quantified no difference in their number between PC-ablated and control larvae could be observed suggesting that ECs in the cerebellum of PC-ablated larvae are generated in appropriate numbers (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A, B).
evidence: This describes quantitative experimental results, supported by figure reference.

claim: ECs in the cerebellum of PC-ablated larvae are generated in appropriate numbers.
source: When green fluorescent ECs were quantified no difference in their number between PC-ablated and control larvae could be observed suggesting that ECs in the cerebellum of PC-ablated larvae are generated in appropriate numbers (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A, B).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the EC quantification data.

claim: At 3 days post-treatment, the average firing frequencies and highest burst frequencies of ECs were significantly elevated upon acute loss of PC inhibitory input.
source: However, at 3 dpt the average firing frequencies and highest burst frequencies of ECs were significantly elevated upon acute loss of PC inhibitory input (Figure 3—figure supplement 4B–D), as ECs may still receive excitatory input from parallel fibers (Hashimoto and Hibi, 2012; Hibi and Shimizu, 2012).
evidence: This describes electrophysiological experimental results, supported by figure reference and citations.

claim: ECs may still receive excitatory input from parallel fibers.
source: However, at 3 dpt the average firing frequencies and highest burst frequencies of ECs were significantly elevated upon acute loss of PC inhibitory input (Figure 3—figure supplement 4B–D), as ECs may still receive excitatory input from parallel fibers (Hashimoto and Hibi, 2012; Hibi and Shimizu, 2012).
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the elevated EC firing, supported by citations.

claim: The elevated EC firing frequency returned to a slight non-significant elevation at 7 days post-treatment during ongoing PC regeneration.
source: This elevated firing frequency returned already at 7 dpt to a slight non-significant elevation during ongoing PC regeneration, and was indistinguishable from ECs in controls from 10 dpt onwards (Figure 3—figure supplement 4B–D).
evidence: This describes electrophysiological experimental results, supported by figure reference.

claim: EC firing frequency was indistinguishable from controls from 10 days post-treatment onwards.
source: This elevated firing frequency returned already at 7 dpt to a slight non-significant elevation during ongoing PC regeneration, and was indistinguishable from ECs in controls from 10 dpt onwards (Figure 3—figure supplement 4B–D).
evidence: This describes electrophysiological experimental results, supported by figure reference.

claim: Regenerating PCs quickly reestablish proper inhibitory input with their direct efferences (ECs).
source: This suggests that regenerating PCs quickly reestablish proper inhibitory input with their direct efferences (Figure 3I).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the EC electrophysiology data.

claim: mCardinal-fluorescent membrane protrusions from regenerating PCs with stronger expression in axons could be determined adjacent to ECs sometimes wrapping around their somata at 10 days post-treatment.
source: Injection of a bicistronic 4xcpce vector (Namikawa et al., 2019b) driving expression of the nuclear located histone2B-tagBFP2 (H2B-tagBFP2) and the membrane-associated mCardinal-CAAX fluorescent reporter proteins into dual transgenic PC-ATTAC/olig2:GFP one cell-stage embryos resulted after PC ablation in some regenerating PCs in which mCardinal-fluorescent membrane protrusions from these regenerating PCs with stronger expression in axons – probably mediated by the C-terminal palmitoylation motif (Steele-Nicholson and Andrews, 2022) – could be determined by confocal microscopy adjacent to ECs sometimes wrapping around their somata at 10 dpt (Figure 3—figure supplement 5A–D).
evidence: This describes anatomical observations from microinjection experiments, supported by figure reference and citation.

claim: The anatomical findings support a fast reestablishment of inhibitory PC to EC neurotransmission by regenerating PCs.
source: These findings support a fast reestablishment of inhibitory PC to EC neurotransmission by regenerating PCs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the anatomical and electrophysiological data.

claim: ECs may adapt in their intrinsic firing properties to the lack of inhibitory PC input to compensate for excessive parallel fiber excitation.
source: Alternatively, ECs adapt in their intrinsic firing properties to the lack of inhibitory PC input to compensate for an excessive parallel fiber excitation.
evidence: This is an alternative explanation for the EC electrophysiology results.

claim: At 2 days post-treatment, the speed of eye movement during object tracking and saccade frequency were reduced compared to controls in the OKR test.
source: At 2 dpt, when PC degeneration is prominent, the speed of eye movement during object tracking and saccade frequency were reduced compared to controls (Figure 4C left panel, D).
evidence: This describes behavioral experimental results, supported by figure reference.

claim: At 10 days post-treatment when on average 29% of PCs had been reestablished, OKR response had recovered.
source: Strikingly, at 10 dpt when on average 29% of PCs had been reestablished (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), OKR response had recovered neither differing in eye movement speed nor in saccade frequency compared to controls (Figure 4C right panel, D).
evidence: This describes behavioral experimental results, supported by figure reference.

claim: At 2 days post-treatment, PC-ablated larvae traveled longer distances at elevated mean and maximum swim speeds suggesting hyperactive behavior.
source: At 2 dpt PC-ablated larvae traveled longer distances at elevated mean and maximum swim speeds suggesting hyperactive behavior, even above EtOH-treated controls (Figure 5D upper row, E).
evidence: This describes behavioral experimental results, supported by figure reference.

claim: Between 9 and 11 days post-treatment when PC replenishment ranged on average around 40%, all swim parameters had recovered.
source: Between 9 and 11 dpt, when PC replenishment ranged on average around 40% (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), all swim parameters had recovered and were not different to all control groups, respectively (Figure 5D lower row).
evidence: This describes behavioral experimental results, supported by figure reference.

claim: At 2 days post-treatment, PC-ablated specimens spent significantly more time swimming along the walls and less frequently entered the open zone of the arena.
source: At 2 dpt PC-ablated specimens spent significantly more time swimming along the walls and less frequently entered the open zone of the arena (Figure 5B, C upper row).
evidence: This describes behavioral experimental results, supported by figure reference.

claim: An increase in thigmotaxis is considered to relate to elevated anxiety.
source: Such an increase in thigmotaxis is considered to relate to elevated anxiety (Richendrfer et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge about behavioral interpretation, supported by citation.

claim: At 9-11 days post-treatment, PC-ablated specimens displayed no significant differences in thigmotaxis compared to all control groups.
source: Again, at 9–11 dpt PC-ablated specimens displayed no significant differences in thigmotaxis compared to all control groups (Figure 5B, C lower row).
evidence: This describes behavioral experimental results, supported by figure reference.

claim: PCs reestablish proper physiological signature after regeneration and regain functional properties within 10 days in controlling visuo-motor, locomotor and thigmotactic functions already at a PC recovery rate around 50%.
source: Together these findings from behavioral analysis show that PCs not only reestablish the proper physiological signature after regeneration, but also regain their functional properties within 10 days in controlling visuo-motor, locomotor and thigmotactic functions already at a PC recovery rate around 50% (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the behavioral and electrophysiological data.

claim: Adult sexually mature zebrafish older than 3 months post-fertilization are considered unable to replace lost PCs, like the mammalian cerebellum.
source: Adult sexually mature zebrafish older than 3 months post-fertilization (mpf) are considered unable to replace lost PCs, like the mammalian cerebellum (Kaslin et al., 2017).
evidence: This describes the prevailing view in the field, supported by citation.

claim: Three consecutive treatments with Endoxifen resulted in higher PC ablation efficiencies in adults compared to 4-OHT.
source: We therefore, induced apoptotic cell death in heterozygous PC-ATTAC adults at 5 months of age (Figure 6A) by three consecutive treatments with Endoxifen, an active metabolite of 4-OHT, which resulted in higher PC ablation efficiencies in adults compared to 4-OHT.
evidence: This describes experimental methodology and results.

claim: Apoptosis of PCs and clearance of debris took longer in adults than in larvae.
source: As apoptosis of PCs and clearance of debris took longer than in larvae, remaining PCs were quantified on consecutive vibratome sections of the CCe at 13–14 dpt (Figure 6C, F), which revealed an ablation efficiency above 90% compared to solvent controls (Figure 7A, B, I).
evidence: This describes experimental observations and results, supported by figure references.

claim: Adult PC ablation efficiency was above 90% compared to solvent controls at 13-14 days post-treatment.
source: As apoptosis of PCs and clearance of debris took longer than in larvae, remaining PCs were quantified on consecutive vibratome sections of the CCe at 13–14 dpt (Figure 6C, F), which revealed an ablation efficiency above 90% compared to solvent controls (Figure 7A, B, I).
evidence: This describes quantitative experimental results, supported by figure references.

claim: In the rostral parts of the adult CCe, PC ablation was nearly complete, while PCs in the caudal part were more resistant to apoptotic ablation.
source: Interestingly, while in the rostral parts of the CCe PC ablation was nearly complete, PCs in the caudal part were more resistant to apoptotic ablation (Figure 6A, C, F).
evidence: This describes spatial patterns in the ablation data, supported by figure references.

claim: At 2 weeks post-treatment, control PC-ATTAC fish displayed strong and continuous red fluorescence from the dorsal surface of their CCe, while in PC-ablated specimens fluorescence was faint at best or completely absent.
source: Fluorescent stereomicroscopy recordings from living fish confirmed the results of PC quantification from fixed tissue. At 2 weeks post-treatment (wpt) control PC-ATTAC fish displayed a strong and continuous red fluorescence from the dorsal surface of their CCe, while in PC-ablated specimens, fluorescence was faint at best, or completely absent (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: This describes in vivo imaging results, supported by figure reference.

claim: At 4 and 12 months post-treatment, a robust cerebellum-derived fluorescence had reappeared covering an increasing area of the CCe.
source: Strikingly, at 4 and 12 mpt a robust cerebellum-derived fluorescence had reappeared covering an increasing area of the CCe (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This describes in vivo imaging results, supported by figure reference.

claim: The fluorescence gradually converged to maximum intensity values obtained from adult controls, suggesting significant PC regeneration.
source: This fluorescence gradually converged to maximum intensity values obtained from adult controls (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, B), suggesting a significant PC regeneration.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the in vivo imaging data.

claim: EGFP fluorescent cells were observed in the CCe of Tg(ptf1a:EGFP) adult fish, showing that a source of progenitor cells for PCs is still present at advanced adult ages.
source: The observation of EGFP fluorescent cells in the CCe of Tg(ptf1a:EGFP) adult fish showed that a source of progenitor cells for PCs is still present at advanced adult ages (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This describes experimental observations, supported by figure reference.

claim: In the adult cerebellum, at least a few differentiated PCs (RFP positive) showed remaining GFP fluorescence derived from ptf1a:GFP progenitors.
source: Furthermore, in the cerebellum of adult double transgenic Tg(ptf1a:EGFP) × Tg(PC-ATTAC) zebrafish, at least a few differentiated PCs (RFP positive) showed remaining GFP fluorescence derived from ptf1a:GFP progenitors providing evidence of ptf1a-expressing cells as progenitors of PCs also in the adult cerebellum (Figure 6—figure supplement 2D, E).
evidence: This describes experimental observations, supported by figure reference.

claim: This provides evidence of ptf1a-expressing cells as progenitors of PCs also in the adult cerebellum.
source: Furthermore, in the cerebellum of adult double transgenic Tg(ptf1a:EGFP) × Tg(PC-ATTAC) zebrafish, at least a few differentiated PCs (RFP positive) showed remaining GFP fluorescence derived from ptf1a:GFP progenitors providing evidence of ptf1a-expressing cells as progenitors of PCs also in the adult cerebellum (Figure 6—figure supplement 2D, E).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the double transgenic data.

claim: At 4 months post-treatment, ZebrinII-expressing PCs with elaborate dendritic trees were distributed throughout a reappearing PC layer, amounting to 28% of PCs found in controls.
source: At 4 mpt ZebrinII-expressing PCs with elaborate dendritic trees were distributed throughout a reappearing PC layer (Figure 6D, G, J) amounting to 28% of PCs found in controls (Figure 7A, B).
evidence: This describes quantitative experimental results, supported by figure references.

claim: At 12 months post-treatment, gaps between PCs had disappeared and ZebrinII-positive PCs were evenly distributed throughout a continuous PC layer.
source: Finally, at 12 mpt in vivo fluorescent stereomicroscopy and immunohistochemistry revealed that gaps between PCs had disappeared and ZebrinII-positive PCs were evenly distributed throughout a continuous PC layer (Figure 6E, H, K).
evidence: This describes experimental observations, supported by figure references.

claim: The size of the PC population 1 year after ablation comprised 30% in numbers compared to solvent controls.
source: Yet, the size of the PC population 1 year after ablation comprised to 30% in numbers compared to solvent controls (Figure 7A, B), which was not due to an overall growth reduction, as the average body length in both fish groups was nearly identical (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This describes quantitative experimental results, supported by figure references.

claim: The reduced PC population size 1 year after ablation was not due to an overall growth reduction, as the average body length in both fish groups was nearly identical.
source: Yet, the size of the PC population 1 year after ablation comprised to 30% in numbers compared to solvent controls (Figure 7A, B), which was not due to an overall growth reduction, as the average body length in both fish groups was nearly identical (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This describes control measurements, supported by figure reference.

claim: PC axon bundles projecting to the vestibular nuclei were completely degenerated at 2 weeks post-treatment, were reestablished at 4 months post-treatment, and formed a prominent cerebello-vestibular tract at 12 months post-treatment.
source: Of note, PC axon bundles projecting directly to the vestibular nuclei (Knogler et al., 2019; Namikawa et al., 2019b), which were completely degenerated at 2 wpt, were reestablished at 4 mpt and formed a prominent cerebello-vestibular tract at 12 mpt (Figure 6—figure supplement 3A–F).
evidence: This describes anatomical observations, supported by figure reference and citations.

claim: Degeneration of the entire PC population in the adult zebrafish cerebellum does not represent an irreversible loss of these principal cerebellar neurons.
source: These findings demonstrate that degeneration of the entire PC population in the adult zebrafish cerebellum does not represent an irreversible loss of these principal cerebellar neurons as previously thought.
evidence: This is a major conclusion of the study, contrasting with previous findings.

claim: The adult zebrafish cerebellum maintains an impressive capability to regenerate significant numbers of PCs counteracting degeneration.
source: Instead, the adult zebrafish cerebellum maintains an impressive capability to regenerate significant numbers of PCs counteracting degeneration.
evidence: This is a major conclusion of the study.

claim: With an average of 8% PC survivors, the caudal area of the adult CCe was more resistant to induced apoptosis than the rostral area.
source: With an average of 8% PC survivors, the caudal area of the adult CCe was more resistant to induced apoptosis than the rostral area, in which PC survival was sparse.
evidence: This describes quantitative analysis of regional differences in ablation.

claim: Medial and caudal regions of the PC layer were more efficient in replenishing lost PCs compared to rostral areas.
source: When PC regeneration in sagittal sections of the CCe was evaluated based on morphological landmarks, medial and caudal regions of the PC layer were more efficient in replenishing lost PCs compared to rostral areas, irrespective of subdividing the CCe into two or three areas (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This describes quantitative analysis of regional differences in regeneration, supported by figure reference.

claim: Patterned PC degeneration and regeneration may reflect the subdivision of the PC layer into different functional subcompartments along the rostro-caudal axis.
source: This patterned PC degeneration and regeneration may reflect the subdivision of the PC layer into different functional subcompartments along the rostro-caudal axis (Knogler et al., 2019; Matsui et al., 2014), and future elucidation of the underlying mechanisms promise to reveal important insights into PC maturation processes.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the regional patterns, supported by citations.

claim: Four different PC subtypes have been distinguished based on soma size correlating with different dendrite morphology and physiology.
source: Recently, four different PC subtypes have been distinguished based on soma size correlating with a different dendrite morphology and physiology, but not being segregated with respect to their location in the PC layer (Chang et al., 2020; Figure 7—figure supplement 1 E).
evidence: This describes previous findings in the literature, supported by citation and figure reference.

claim: Compared to PCs in controls, apoptosis-resistant and regenerating PCs contained on average a larger soma size in all areas of the CCe.
source: By measuring the size of PC somata all PC subtypes could be identified during de- and regeneration. Yet, compared to PCs in controls, apoptosis-resistant and regenerating PCs contained on average a larger soma size in all areas of the CCe, independent of subdividing the PC layer into two or three rostro-caudal compartments (Figure 7—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This describes quantitative analysis of PC soma size, supported by figure reference.

claim: In all rostro-caudal cerebellar compartments, PCs with a large soma diameter (>10 µm) were significantly overrepresented at 2 weeks post-treatment.
source: A simple explanation for this finding is that PCs in a depleted PC population use the available space for increasing in size. Alternatively, remnant PCs grow in size because of plasticity processes with PCs trying to recover as many functions as possible. Another explanation may be that the observed difference in PC soma distribution reflects a difference in resilience of PC subtypes to neurodegenerative processes or a different regenerative potential among PC subtypes. Addressing these questions by establishing the proper technical tools for investigating the regional as well as the subtype differences in PC regeneration represent future rewarding experimental goals to reveal further the mechanistic concepts and limitations of PC regeneration in the adult cerebellum.
evidence: This describes quantitative analysis and offers multiple interpretations.

claim: The overrepresentation of large soma PCs was maintained but less pronounced during regeneration up to 1 year.
source: A simple explanation for this finding is that PCs in a depleted PC population use the available space for increasing in size. Alternatively, remnant PCs grow in size because of plasticity processes with PCs trying to recover as many functions as possible. Another explanation may be that the observed difference in PC soma distribution reflects a difference in resilience of PC subtypes to neurodegenerative processes or a different regenerative potential among PC subtypes.
evidence: This describes temporal patterns in the soma size data.

claim: The anterior CCe that is most sensitive to apoptotic PC ablation displayed the largest percentage of PCs with a soma diameter above 10 µm, ranging on average between 83% and 92% of the entire PC content.
source: Noteworthy, the anterior CCe that is most sensitive to apoptotic PC ablation, displayed the largest percentage of PCs with a soma diameter above 10 µm, ranging on average between 83% and 92% of the entire PC content (area 1, Figure 7E).
evidence: This describes quantitative analysis of regional and subtype patterns, supported by figure reference.

claim: Strong adapting subtype I PCs are more resilient to apoptotic cell death induction compared to PC subtypes II-IV.
source: These findings suggest that strong adapting subtype I PCs are more resilient to apoptotic cell death induction compared to PC subtypes II–IV.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the soma size distribution data.

claim: Based on soma size measurements, PCs with larger somata were overrepresented in the cerebellum with regenerating PCs compared to PCs in control larvae.
source: To address if such differences in PC subtype regeneration are already present during larval stages, we reanalyzed the cerebellum of zebrafish larvae after PC ablation. Indeed, based on soma size measurements, PCs with larger somata were overrepresented in the cerebellum with regenerating PCs compared to PCs in control larvae (Figure 7—figure supplement 2) suggesting that PC subtypes inherently possess different regeneration abilities already during PC differentiation stages.
evidence: This describes reanalysis of larval data, supported by figure reference.

claim: PC subtypes inherently possess different regeneration abilities already during PC differentiation stages.
source: To address if such differences in PC subtype regeneration are already present during larval stages, we reanalyzed the cerebellum of zebrafish larvae after PC ablation. Indeed, based on soma size measurements, PCs with larger somata were overrepresented in the cerebellum with regenerating PCs compared to PCs in control larvae (Figure 7—figure supplement 2) suggesting that PC subtypes inherently possess different regeneration abilities already during PC differentiation stages.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the larval soma size data.

claim: Adult PC loss is known to result in compromised exploration.
source: Functional PC regeneration implies the restoration of behavior caused by adult PC loss known to result in a compromised exploration (Buchberger et al., 2021; Elsaey et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to existing literature.

claim: Shortly after ablation, despite the massive PC loss, zebrafish showed no significant difference in mean swim speed or total distance traveled compared to solvent-treated siblings.
source: Shortly after ablation despite the massive PC loss, zebrafish showed no significant difference neither in their mean swim speed nor in the total distance traveled compared to solvent-treated siblings (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This describes behavioral experimental results, supported by figure reference.

claim: Zebrafish can largely relinquish PCs for locomotive control under non-strenuous conditions.
source: This confirmed previous findings that zebrafish can largely relinquish PCs for locomotive control under non-strenuous conditions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the behavioral data, consistent with previous findings.

claim: Specimens with acute PC degeneration (2 weeks post-treatment) and during PC regeneration (4 months post-treatment) hardly ever entered the upper half of the new tank and displayed significantly reduced exploratory behavior compared to controls.
source: In contrast, specimens with acute PC degeneration (2 wpt) as well as during PC regeneration (4 mpt) hardly ever entered the upper half of the new tank and displayed a significantly reduced exploratory behavior compared to controls (Figure 7F, G).
